title: Magellan - Discovery: migration OpenAI -> Dedicated
topics: migration path from OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery for Magellan Systems exploring migration from OpenAI hosted usage to Redwood Dedicated. Key concerns: eval parity, tokenization/model drift, latency vs cost, VPC and KMS requirements, and a concrete POC to run benchmarks using their TGI/vLLM-based stack. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pricing and benchmark guide, Magellan to send sample prompt set and security questionnaire; schedule a deep-dive SE demo and a pilot benchmarking window.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-10-13 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57 mins | Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jared (CTO - Magellan), Maya (ML Eng), Alex (Security), Samir (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining - appreciate you carving time. quick intro from our side: I'm Evan, AE for enterprise west, with Priya who'll cover the technical stuff.
[00:12] Jared (Magellan - CTO): Hey Evan, thanks. Jared here; Maya, Alex, Samir with me. We're about 35 people on infra/ml, mostly using OpenAI for prod and a mix of vLLM and TGI for local inference. We're exploring Dedicated to lower costs and get better control.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Awesome. Can you walk us through current usage patterns - qps, request sizes, seq lengths, typical latencies you're seeing from OpenAI?
[00:35] Maya (Magellan): Sure. Average payloads are short, 50-150 tokens, but we do have episodic long-context batches up to 8k tokens for conversational history. Right now p95 is around 800ms with OpenAI gpt-4-ish calls, cost is spiking as we scale. We also run a local inference layer with vLLM for edge cases, and sometimes TGI backends for custom quantized LLMs.
[00:58] Evan: Got it. So the migration question is twofold: first, parity - will model outputs match what you get from OpenAI (or close enough), and second, ops - networking, VPC, KMS, RBAC. Also performance: latency/throughput and unit cost.
[01:12] Jared: Exactly. The business asks, can we switch without user-visible regressions. Also security: we need SOC 2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and preferably bring-your-own KMS.
[01:25] Priya: All standard. Redwood Dedicated supports private control plane and customer-managed networking; KMS integrations are available. For parity, we usually recommend a small eval where you run identical prompts against OpenAI, Redwood hosted, and Dedicated (same model family/weights if you choose an open checkpoint). We also pay attention to tokenization differences - that bit often sneaks up on folks.
[01:45] Maya: Tokenization - yes. We've hit issues where the token counts/stop sequences differ between providers, causing subtle output drift. How do you surface that?
[01:53] Priya: We include tokenization normalization in the benchmark harness. For example, if you're using tiktoken vs HF GPT tokenizer differences, we normalize the input and compare outputs with fuzz metrics, edit distance, and task-level evals (e.g., accuracy on downstream tasks).
[02:10] Alex (Security): On compliance: can you confirm where logs live for Dedicated? We need to prove no customer PII leaves the VPC and that audit logs are retained for 90 days.
[02:20] Evan: Dedicated keeps logs in the customer's VPC by default for Private deployments; for Redwood Dedicated (hosted dedicated), we offer configurable retention and encrypted audit logs. We can pull our SOC 2 and ISO docs - we'll share those.
[02:33] Samir (Product): Curious about compatibility with our vLLM/TGI tooling. We have a lot of in-house scripts that spin up vLLM locally and sometimes call TGI endpoints. Do you support the same model formats?
[02:44] Priya: Yes, we support common formats - HF transformers checkpoints, GGML conversions, and containerized TGI backends for some workflows. If you're running quantized weights optimized for vLLM, we can advise on conversion profiles. There's sometimes a perf delta, but the runtime can be tuned - kernel selection, sequence packing, etc.
[03:02] Maya: When you say perf delta, what magnitude? We saw up to 20-30% throughput differences when switching kernels last time.
[03:08] Priya: It depends on model architecture and quantization. For 8-bit quantized small LLMs, differences are usually within 5-15% with proper kernel selection. For large long-context models, if you switch execution paths (e.g., different attention kernels), you might see larger swings. That's why we run benchmarks with your prompt distribution.
[03:28] Jared: Ok. On the POC: what's the typical scope and duration? We're thinking 2-4 weeks to validate parity and cost.
[03:36] Evan: That's common. Week 1: onboarding + security review; Week 2: run benchmark harness (your prompts) on Dedicated in a staging VPC; Week 3: analyze results and tune; Week 4: optional canary in production. We'll provide a benchmark guide and a small infra template.
[03:51] Alex: Regarding SAML/SSO and RBAC - we have an internal requirement to integrate with Okta and maintain audit trails. Can Redwood integrate with Okta for user roles?
[04:01] Evan: Yes, SAML/Okta integration is supported; RBAC maps to your identity groups and we surface role-based audit logs. We'll attach our integration guide.
[04:09] Maya: A more subtle thing - evaluation parity on few-shot tasks. OpenAI's temperature/decoding differences make exact replication hard. Do you have techniques to match outputs?
[04:19] Priya: We recommend deterministic decoding settings where possible, seed control, and matching sampling parameters. For larger differences, we run head-to-head evals and use a tolerance threshold: if task accuracy is equal or better, minor token-level diffs are acceptable. For cases where exact reproduction is critical, we can pin model weights to the same open checkpoint.
[04:39] Jared: How do you handle model fallbacks? If we have Dedicated and a hosted capacity for overflow, can requests automatically route?
[04:48] Evan: Yes - smart routing policies are available: latency-first, cost-first, or region-first. You can configure automatic fallback to Redwood hosted or a lower-cost quantized variant if dedicated capacity is saturated.
[05:00] Samir: Pricing question - how does Dedicated pricing compare vs hosted as we scale? We're trying to model per-inference unit economics.
[05:07] Evan: Dedicated is commit-based (monthly/annual). You get reserved GPU pools and lower per-token costs. For typical production workloads, customers see 30-60% reduction versus pure hosted spend depending on utilization. We'll send a modeled pricing spreadsheet with scenarios.
[05:20] Maya: For the benchmark, we want to include our TGI quantized model and results from our vLLM runs. Is Redwood able to ingest those artifacts and run the same workload?
[05:29] Priya: Yes - we can accept your model artifacts and either run them on a Redwood node or help convert them to our supported layout. If you prefer, we can run a side-by-side using your vLLM stack vs Redwood runtime on identical hardware profiles.
[05:41] Alex: Data residency - some customers need EU-only processing. Can Dedicated be region-locked?
[05:46] Evan: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned in a specific cloud region or even on-prem/private deployment for stricter residency. We'll flag options in the SOW.
[05:56] Jared: One operational ask: do you support KV/prefix caching to reduce cost for repeated prompts? We do a lot of system prompts and prefix reuse.
[06:03] Priya: Absolutely - Redwood has prefix and KV caching features that can be tuned per route. That often leads to big unit-cost wins for chat-style workloads.
[06:12] Maya: Great. A few quick gotchas we've seen: differences in tokenization, stop token handling, and behavior with function-calling APIs. How mature is your function-calling feature?
[06:22] Priya: We support structured output and function calling patterns; though names may differ we provide SDK helpers to normalize the interface. We'll share docs and examples.
[06:31] Evan: Want to talk about next steps? From Redwood's side we'll: 1) share pricing spreadsheet and SOW template, 2) send SOC2/ISO security pack, 3) provide benchmark harness and onboarding checklist.
[06:43] Jared: From Magellan: we'll send a sample prompt set + anonymized logs, security questionnaire answers, and a list of models/artifacts (TGI/vLLM checkpoints) we want to test. We're aiming to start the POC by Oct 25.
[06:56] Priya: Cool. On the technical deep-dive - should we schedule a SE-only session to go over converting your TGI artifacts and running vLLM parity tests?
[07:04] Maya: Yes please, that's critical. Also would like to benchmark latency p95 at our typical provisioned QPS (we can include load profile).
[07:12] Samir: Can you also include a quick note on expected infra changes? We're trying to map networking/VPC needs to our infra roadmap.
[07:18] Evan: We'll include the infra template.
[07:20] Alex: One last sec on encryption: for BYOK KMS, do you support HSM-backed keys?
[07:26] Priya: Yes, HSM/KMS integrations supported - we'll outline options and operational flow for key rotation and audit.
[07:33] Jared: Perfect. If we can validate parity and security baseline, we can move to commit.
[07:38] Evan: Thanks all. I'll do a quick recap and owners.
[07:41] Evan (recap): Next steps: Redwood to send pricing/benchmark guide/SOC2 pack (Evan). Magellan to share prompt set, logs, model artifacts (Jared/Maya). Schedule SE deep-dive for TGI/vLLM conversion week of Oct 19 (Priya to own scheduling). Aim to start POC week of Oct 25.
[07:58] Maya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:01] Jared: Thanks.
[08:05] Evan: Appreciate it, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
[08:09] Meeting ends.
